results.title: $p$-soluble groups (series with $p$- and $p'$-factors)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is $p$-soluble when it has a chain of subgroups $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$, each normal in the next, such that for every $i < n$ the relative index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ (taken to be $0$ when it is infinite) is a power of $p$ or is coprime to $p$. For a finite group this says that every factor $H_{i+1}/H_i$ is a $p$-group or a $p'$-group.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 17.111 (supplements of maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, asked by A. N. Skiba, that for every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ whose order is divisible by $p$ and every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$, if every maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ has a $p$-soluble supplement in $G$, that is, a $p$-soluble subgroup $K$ of $G$ with $MK = G$, then $G$ is $p$-soluble.

results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite group whose order is divisible by $p$, and $P$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. If every maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ has a $p$-soluble supplement in $G$, that is, a $p$-soluble subgroup $K$ of $G$ with $MK = G$, then $G$ is $p$-soluble.

results.title: Fermat-type characterizations of twin primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ be odd, and suppose neither $n$ nor $n + 2$ is a Carmichael number. Then $n$ and $n + 2$ are both prime if and only if $2a^{n+1} \equiv (n + 2)\,a^2 - n \pmod{n(n + 2)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $n(n + 2)$; and $n$ and $n + 2$ are both prime if and only if $n\,a^{n+1} \equiv (n + 2)\,a^{n-1} - 2 \pmod{n(n + 2)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $n(n + 2)$.

results.title: Alahmadi–Luca theorem on Carmichael numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every odd prime $p$, the number $2^n p + 1$ is not a Carmichael number.

results.title: Fermat-type characterizations of Sophie Germain primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. Then $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime if and only if $a^{2p} \equiv (2p + 1)\,a^{p+1} - 2p \pmod{p(2p + 1)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $p(2p + 1)$; and $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime if and only if $(2p + 1)\,a^{p-1} \equiv p\,a^{2p} + p + 1 \pmod{p(2p + 1)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $p(2p + 1)$.

results.title: Fermat-type congruences along a Sophie Germain prime chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ and $j$ be natural numbers and put $q_{i+1} = 2^i (p + 1) - 1$ for $i \ge 0$, so that $q_1 = p$ and $q_{i+2} = 2q_{i+1} + 1$. Suppose $q_1, \dots, q_{j+2}$ are all prime, and write $q = q_{j+1}$ and $q' = q_{j+2} = 2q + 1$. Then for every integer $a$ coprime to $qq'$, $a^{q'-1} \equiv q'\,a^{q+1} - 2q \pmod{qq'}$ and $q'\,a^{q-1} \equiv q\,a^{q'-1} + q + 1 \pmod{qq'}$.

results.title: Length of a Sophie Germain prime chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\mathrm{ord}_p(2)$ be the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo $p$. Then there is some $j \le \mathrm{ord}_p(2)$ such that $2^j (p + 1) - 1$ is not prime. Thus the Sophie Germain prime chain $q_1 = p$, $q_{i+1} = 2q_i + 1 = 2^i (p + 1) - 1$ begins with at most $\mathrm{ord}_p(2)$ consecutive primes.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a smooth manifold $M$ and $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, $\mathcal{G}^k(M)$ is the space of all smooth Riemannian metrics on $M$, equipped with the $C^k$ topology. It is not the space of $C^k$ metrics: every element is smooth, and $k$ only indexes the topology.

results.title: Constant rescalings converge in every $C^k$ topology
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $M$, and let $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. Let $l$ be a filter on a type $\alpha$ and let $c_a > 0$ ($a \in \alpha$) be positive reals with $c_a \to 1$ along $l$. Then the rescaled metrics $c_a g$ tend to $g$ along $l$ in the $C^k$ topology.

results.title: A holomorphic function not identically zero has finitely many zeros in a disc
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P \in \mathbb{C}$ and $r > 0$, write $D(P,r)$ for the open disc and $\overline{D}(P,r)$ for the closed disc of center $P$ and radius $r$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on some open set containing $\overline{D}(P,r)$. If $f$ does not vanish identically on $D(P,r)$, then $f$ has only finitely many zeros in $D(P,r)$.

results.title: Van der Waerden's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all positive integers $r$ and $k$ there is a natural number $N$ such that for every coloring of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ with $r$ colors there are natural numbers $a \ge 1$ and $d \ge 1$ with $a + (k - 1)d \le N$ such that each of the $k$ terms $a, a + d, \dots, a + (k - 1)d$ has the same color as $a$.

results.title: Reduction of a binary word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The reduction $\operatorname{red}(w)$ of a binary word $w$ is the word obtained by collapsing each maximal run of equal consecutive letters of $w$ to a single letter; for example $\operatorname{red}(0011101) = 0101$.

results.title: Alternations of a binary word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of alternations of a binary word $w$ is the number of occurrences of the factors $01$ and $10$ in $w$, that is, the number of positions $i$ with $w_i \ne w_{i+1}$.

results.title: Extension of the Thue–Morse substitution to binary words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The morphism $\mu$ sends each letter to a word of length two, $\mu(0) = 01$ and $\mu(1) = 10$, and a binary word $w_1 w_2 \cdots w_k$ to the concatenation $\mu(w_1) \mu(w_2) \cdots \mu(w_k)$.

results.title: Regular paperfolding sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The regular paperfolding sequence $f = f_0 f_1 f_2 \cdots$ over $\{0, 1\}$ is indexed from $0$: for each $i$, write $i + 1 = m \cdot 2^k$ with $m$ odd; then $f_i = 0$ if $m \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and $f_i = 1$ if $m \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.

results.title: Reduced factor complexity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite binary word $w$, let $\mathrm{red}(w)$ be the word obtained from $w$ by collapsing each run of equal letters to a single letter. For an infinite binary word $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ and a natural number $n$, the reduced factor complexity $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_x(n)$ is the number of distinct words $\mathrm{red}(w)$ as $w$ ranges over the length-$n$ factors of $x$.

results.title: Reduced abelian complexity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a binary sequence $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the reduced abelian complexity $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_x(n)$ is the number of distinct pairs $(|\mathrm{red}(v)|, |\mathrm{red}(v)|_0)$, where $v$ ranges over the length-$n$ factors of $x$, $\mathrm{red}(v)$ is the reduction of $v$ (each run of equal letters collapsed to a single letter) and $|w|_0$ is the number of letters $0$ in $w$.…

results.title: Minimum number of alternations in Thue–Morse factors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $m_n$ is the least number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$n$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence.

results.title: Maximum number of alternations in Thue–Morse factors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $M_n$ is the largest number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$n$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence.

results.title: Alternations of the Thue–Morse image of a word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be the morphism on binary words with $\mu(0) = 01$ and $\mu(1) = 10$. If $w$ is a nonempty binary word of length $|w|$ with $\alpha$ alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ), then $\mu(w)$ has exactly $2|w| - 1 - \alpha$ alternations.

results.title: Doubling recurrences for Thue–Morse alternation extrema
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, let $m_k$ and $M_k$ be the least and the largest number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$k$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence. Then for every $n \ge 2$, $m_{2n} = 2n - 1 - M_{n+1}$, $M_{2n} = 2n - 1 - m_n$, $m_{2n+1} = 2n - M_{n+1}$ and $M_{2n+1} = 2n - m_{n+1}$.

results.title: Quadrupling recurrences for Thue–Morse alternation extrema
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, let $m_k$ and $M_k$ be the least and the largest number of alternations (positions where two adjacent letters differ) among the length-$k$ factors of the Thue–Morse sequence. Then for every $n \ge 1$, $m_{4n} = 2n - 1 + m_{n+1}$, $M_{4n} = 2n + M_{n+1}$, $m_{4n+2} = 2n + m_{n+1}$ and $M_{4n+2} = 2n + 1 + M_{n+1}$.

results.title: Reduced complexity of the Thue–Morse word at odd lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be the Thue–Morse sequence and $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t$ its reduced factor complexity. For every odd natural number $n$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(n) = \rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t((n+1)/2)$.

results.title: Reduced complexity of the Thue–Morse word at even lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be the Thue–Morse sequence and $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t$ its reduced factor complexity. For every natural number $m \ge 1$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(4m) = \rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(m+1) + 2$, and for every natural number $m \ge 0$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(4m+2) = \rho^{\mathrm{red}}_t(m+1) + 2$.

Then the reduction of $w$, the word obtained by collapsing each maximal run of equal letters of $w$ to a single letter, has length $n + 1$; that is, $w$ has exactly $n + 1$…

results.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at even lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every $n \ge 1$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(2n) = 4$.

results.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 8n + 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every $n \ge 1$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(8n+1) = 4$.

results.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 8n + 3
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every natural number $n$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(8n+3) = 6$.

results.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 8n + 5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every natural number $n$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(8n+5) = 6$.

results.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 8n + 7
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every natural number $n$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(8n+7) = 6$.

results.title: Reduced complexity of the paperfolding word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n)$ be the number of distinct reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$. For every $n \ge 2$, $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n) = 4$ if $n \equiv 0, 1, 2, 4$ or $6 \pmod 8$, and $\rho^{\mathrm{red}}_f(n) = 6$ if $n \equiv 3, 5$ or $7 \pmod 8$.

results.title: Reduced abelian complexity of the paperfolding word at even lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n)$ be the number of reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$, counted up to rearrangement of their letters. For every even $n > 0$, $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n) = 3$.

results.title: Reduced abelian complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 1 mod 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n)$ be the number of reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$, counted up to rearrangement of their letters. For every $n > 1$ with $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n) = 4$.

results.title: Reduced abelian complexity of the paperfolding word at lengths 3 mod 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the regular paperfolding sequence and let $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n)$ be the number of reductions of length-$n$ factors of $f$, counted up to rearrangement of their letters. For every natural number $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, $\rho^{\mathrm{ab,red}}_f(n) = 5$.

results.title: Instances of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the degree bound).

results.title: Well-formed DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is well formed when $n > 0$, the list $E$ has no repeated entries, and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, with the reversed pair $(v, u)$ not in $E$.

results.title: Feasibility for DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is feasible when there is a list $T$ of pairs of natural numbers such that $T$ is a sublist of $E$ (obtained by deleting entries and keeping the order), $T$ has no repeated entries, $T$ has exactly $n - 1$ entries, the graph of $T$ on $n$ vertices is connected, and for every vertex $v < n$ there is no sublist of $T$ with $K + 1$ entries each of which has…

results.title: DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when bitstring decoding of $x$ as a triple $(n, E, K)$ succeeds and returns an instance of DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE that is both well formed and feasible; every bitstring that does not decode is rejected.

results.title: DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem DEGREE-CONSTRAINED SPANNING TREE belongs to the class NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
